title: ChatGPT suggests tethered cord syndrome for a child seen by 17 doctors over three years; pediatric neurosurgeon confirms and operates
summary: Mother entered son's MRI notes and symptoms into ChatGPT; it suggested tethered cord syndrome, confirmed and operated on by a neurosurgeon.
account: In 2023 Courtney, mother of Alex, a boy whose chronic pain began at age 4 during the COVID-19 lockdown and who went on to grind his teeth, stop growing taller and drag his left foot, entered his MRI notes and symptom observations line by line into ChatGPT after 17 physicians over three years had not produced a diagnosis. ChatGPT suggested tethered cord syndrome. She booked a new neurosurgeon, Dr Holly Gilmer of the Michigan Head & Spine Institute, who reviewed the MRI, identified spina bifida occulta with a tethered cord, and operated to release the cord a few weeks before the TODAY.com report (first published 11 September 2023, updated 12 September 2023); Alex was still recovering. The month of the ChatGPT query and the surgery date are not given.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant built to answer user prompts; producing a diagnostic hypothesis from entered clinical notes is an instance of that general function, not a designed or validated medical capability.
segment: Caregiver-initiated use of a consumer LLM
taxonomy_note: Closest fit: a caregiver obtained a diagnostic hypothesis directly from a consumer tool after three years in which the health system had not provided one; 'Improved Knowledge Discovery' is the alternative. the date observed is the report date because the article gives no dates for the query or surgery.

ratings.reason: A child with three years of chronic pain, mobility problems and growth delay received a diagnosis and corrective spinal surgery; the report describes him as recovering, so the benefit is life-changing but not shown to be life-saving.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT produced the hypothesis (tethered cord syndrome) that the mother took to a new neurosurgeon; the diagnosis itself was made by the neurosurgeon from the existing MRI and the treatment was surgical. ChatGPT's contribution was to end the diagnostic search; the source is a news report quoting the mother and the treating neurosurgeon, not a peer-reviewed case report.
